failure.implementation_issue: v1.0.1 mixed child did not catch SuspectFF and invoke inherited re-identification path, so the whole run aborted.

comparison_to_prior_trigger.interpretation: The 37 C room-setpoint stimulus is not an unconditional burner-start command. It produced a startup in the prior thermal/controller state but no burner/GFA activity in this run before the transport FF.

conclusions: The production-VS1 compatibility fix worked: the live path reached the controller, verified 20C2/P80=20, wrote only the bounded temporary 0x2306=37 stimulus, and restored the original 21 C value.
No burner startup was captured: all 32 complete mixed rounds remained P84=00, P87=00, both independent flame indicators false, lockout false, and fine GFA control value zero.
The same 37 C stimulus had previously produced P84=02 within 4.793 s, so it is a demand stimulus whose effect depends on current controller/thermal conditions rather than a direct burner command.
The run failed because a known sporadic FF on P87 was not handled by the mixed child, not because of a restore or controller fault.

corrective_action.change: Catch inherited SuspectFF, reject current round, perform full inherited P300/P80 re-identification, reset transition history across the gap, continue if the remaining bounded window permits.
corrective_action.additional_summary: Emit STARTUP_ACTIVITY_SEEN yes/no so a clean null observation is not confused with a captured burner start.
